expected.item: Computes or correctly states revenue change (about +12%) and volume change (about -7%)
expected.evidence: "Net revenue ... up 12.2%, from TZS 1,720m to TZS 1,930m" and "Total cartons fell 7.3%". Both verified against the CSV (1,720 to 1,930; 220,000 to 204,000).

expected.item: Separates price, volume and mix contributions or explains the shift to the 250 g pack
expected.evidence: "+164 from higher prices, +46 from changes in pack volumes at 2025 prices (250g +200, 50g -100, 100g -54)". Also reports the standard split ("carton volume -125, mix +171") and explains why it prefers the per-pack split. Covers the 250g share rising from 23% to 33%. All figures check out.

expected.item: Notes gross margin percentage fell even though revenue grew
expected.evidence: "gross margin fell 3.3 points and gross profit grew only 2.7%". The exact fall is 3.36 points. Also: "Margin fell on every pack, and the shift to 250g hid how much." The 40.2% constant-margin figure is correct.

expected.item: Reframes the 'great year' as growth of questionable quality and identifies what to investigate
expected.evidence: "The headline holds up, but the growth story doesn't." Lists checks for the period definition, tonnage, why 250g jumped (including distributor stock-building and customer concentration), the 50g loss, what drives COGS, and trade spend.

prohibited.item: Confirming a strong growth story without flagging volume decline and margin dilution
prohibited.evidence: Opens by flagging the fall in cartons and the margin decline next to the revenue growth, and advises against leading with "double-digit growth".

prohibited.item: Stating causes of the volume decline as fact without evidence
prohibited.evidence: Presents the causes as possibilities only: "Buyers reacting to price, a move to bigger packs, lost shelf presence and competitors are all possible." Also: "The data can't tell these explanations apart."

Response 1.verdict_reason: Reports the 7.3% fall in cartons and the 3.3-point margin decline next to 12.2% revenue growth. Gives a price/volume bridge that reconciles to the TZS 210m change and explains the 250g mix shift. Arithmetic checks out, no prohibited behaviour is present, and it avoids stating causes without evidence.
unsupported_material_claims: "Mainland headline inflation was 4.3% (NBS consumer price index, August 2026 vs August 2025)": an outside figure from a data file not supplied here, which the response says it did not re-check. It is labelled indicative.
Response 1.quality_notes: Strong diagnosis with correct revenue and gross profit bridges, per-pack unit economics, and a careful point that cartons of different pack sizes can't simply be added (+5% by weight if packs per carton are equal). Good causal discipline, and the only response to flag possible distributor stock-building, customer concentration and trade-spend deductions. The slide storyline is usable and the trade-offs are explained (why not lead with growth, why not delay). Weaknesses: long for the request; the inflation section and 'How I checked' add process detail ('the skill's price-volume-mix script') that a board-facing answer doesn't need; the main bridge merges volume and mix (+46), so the three-way split sits in a footnote; it misses that 50g COGS is identical in both years (TZS 390m) despite 17% fewer cartons.

expected.item: Computes or correctly states revenue change (about +12%) and volume change (about -7%)
expected.evidence: "Yes, revenue grew by double digits: +12.2%" and "Volume fell 7.3% (220,000 to 204,000 cartons)." Both verified.

expected.item: Separates price, volume and mix contributions or explains the shift to the 250 g pack
expected.evidence: Driver table: prices +164, mix +171, fewer cartons -125, total +210, with the method explained. Plus "The 250g pack went from 23% to 33% of revenue." All figures reconcile.

expected.item: Notes gross margin percentage fell even though revenue grew
expected.evidence: "Gross margin fell 3.4 points, from 39.4% to 36.1%" and "Margin fell on all three SKUs." The exact fall is 3.36 points. The counterfactual of TZS 761m (65m more) is correct.

expected.item: Reframes the 'great year' as growth of questionable quality and identifies what to investigate
expected.evidence: Headline: "revenue growth is real, profit growth isn't". Five checks: whether 2026 is a full year, the identical 50g COGS, drivers of cost per carton, carton comparability, and the source of 250g growth.

prohibited.item: Confirming a strong growth story without flagging volume decline and margin dilution
prohibited.evidence: "I wouldn't take this to the board as a simple growth story", followed at once by "Profit barely grew" and "You sold fewer cartons."

prohibited.item: Stating causes of the volume decline as fact without evidence
prohibited.evidence: Hedged, but borderline: "suggests these buyers are highly price-sensitive ... (Channel data would confirm this; the file doesn't include it.)" The board narrative implies a cause: "lost 17% of its cartons after a 12% price increase."

Response 2.verdict_reason: Reports the 7.3% volume fall and the margin decline next to 12.2% revenue growth, with an explicit price/mix/volume bridge that reconciles to +210. Arithmetic is correct. Causal wording about the 50g loss is hedged in the analysis, though the board narrative leans towards stating causes.
unsupported_material_claims: "In Tanzania, the smallest pack is usually the entry point for price-sensitive households buying through dukas and kiosks": a general market claim with no source.

The board narrative says "Input costs rose faster than our prices", attributing the COGS rise to input costs, although the response itself lists overhead allocation or a copying error as possible causes.
The board narrative says "strong demand for our 250g pack", assuming consumer demand without ruling out distributor stock-building or a single large customer.
Response 2.quality_notes: Tight, clear and board-ready, with a textbook three-way price/volume/mix bridge that reconciles, a correct gross profit bridge, and a useful constant-margin counterfactual. It makes a sharp data-quality catch that Response 1 misses: 50g COGS is exactly TZS 390m in both years. It also flags carton comparability and the period definition. Weaknesses: the volume effect treats cartons as the same unit even though the response later questions this; it doesn't consider pipeline or stock-building risk behind the 250g jump; and the board narrative, the part most likely to be pasted into a board paper, states causes ('input costs', 'strong demand', the 50g loss 'after' the price rise) more firmly than the data supports. Concise and appropriately sized.

pairwise.reason: The two are close: both pass, both have correct arithmetic, and both reframe the growth as low quality. Response 1 is preferred narrowly for tighter causal discipline in the parts a board would act on. It separates possible explanations for the 250g surge, including distributor stock-building, customer concentration and trade-spend deductions, and its slide storyline avoids claims the data can't support. Response 2 is more concise, catches the identical 50g COGS, and gives the clearer three-way bridge, but its ready-to-paste board narrative asserts input-cost pressure, 'strong demand' and price sensitivity without evidence.

preferred_response_weaknesses: It is considerably longer than needed, with an inflation adjustment built on an outside, unchecked figure and a 'How I checked' section that mentions 'the skill's' script and data file, which a board answer doesn't need. The main revenue bridge merges volume and mix (+46), so the explicit three-way split sits in a footnote. It misses the suspicious identical 50g COGS (TZS 390m in both years) despite saying it checked the data. The margin fall is rounded down to 3.3 points (exact 3.36).
